title: How Leaders Unwittingly Create Entitlement
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article argues that workplace entitlement is manufactured by leaders, not an innate trait people bring with them, tracing it directly to a pattern of rewarding people without tying recognition to actual merit or measurable contribution. It explains the mechanism: leaders eager to be liked lower expectations, avoid critical feedback, and dole out promotions and perks indiscriminately to boost short-term morale, which trains people to expect more regardless of performance. The piece describes the downstream damage vividly — plummeting productivity alongside rising complaints — and frames the fix as a return to basic management fundamentals: transparent goals, merit-tied rewards, consistent feedback, and real accountability for underperformance.
points: Entitlement is framed as an organizational disease caused by leadership behavior, not an innate trait people arrive with.
The core mechanism is leaders rewarding people to boost morale or likability without tying recognition to measurable contribution.
Once entitlement takes hold, productivity drops sharply while complaints about remaining expectations rise.
The fix is a return to fundamentals: transparent goals, merit-tied rewards, consistent feedback, and real accountability.
quotes: When they fail to tie their caring and rewards to measurable goals, a sense of entitlement is usually the result.
Entitlement is an organizational disease caused by leaders. People learn to be entitled. They don’t show up that way. They simply respond to how they are treated.

Leaders who fall into this trap often do so to increase morale and job satisfaction. To gain favor, they lower expectations, avoid giving critical feedback, recognize people for mediocre work, and provide special accommodations and treatment to anyone who asks for it.
Productivity drops like an anchor, while complaining about whatever expectations still exist goes up.
Entitlement can’t exist when standards and expectations for performance remain high and the most deserving team members receive the hard-won recognition they have earned.
